[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women%27s_marathon&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Qualification")]

## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
Hassan was born in [Adama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama "Adama"), [Oromia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromia "Oromia"), Ethiopia and raised in the countryside of [Kersa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kersa,_Arsi "Kersa, Arsi") in the [Munesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munesa "Munesa") district of the [Arsi Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsi_Zone "Arsi Zone") of Oromia.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-23) She was a recreational runner there. She left her home country as a refugee and arrived in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 2008 at age 15.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-25) She began running while undertaking studies to become a nurse.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-26) She is an [Arsi Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsi_Oromo "Arsi Oromo").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-27)
Hassan became a Dutch citizen in 2013.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-28)
## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2011–2012")]

She got her first spikes and kit from Yke Schouwstra. After she moved to Eindhoven, she met Ton van Hoesel who coached her for two years. In Arnhem, Hassan became a member of the Papendal national training centre for top athletes.
